svg.font-family: Segoe UI, Inter, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: Saksham IQ — the whole system, end to end
A child opens the site and is taught. This is every hop between those two facts: which box is a language model, which is pure Python, where the
fence between them runs, and which single path is allowed to move a star. Every box named here is a real module in this repository.
pure Python — deterministic
reaches a language model
gate, guardrail or kill switch
PostgreSQL — the durable truth
the client (decides nothing)
an outside service
1 · THE CLIENTS
they render a turn and report what the child did; they decide nothing
Web · Next.js (frontend/)
THE SURFACE THE TEAM RUNS
/ and /home send a signed-in child straight to /ai-teacher, and /class redirects
there too - a child is never asked to pick a level. A guest gets the sign-up hub
instead. AppShell wraps every screen and ScheduleStrip rides above all of them,
so the day's plan is visible wherever the child is.
/ai-teacher — the class itself
ONE TEACHING LOOP
page.tsx runs one loop and knows no pedagogy: narrate `speech`, draw the question
large, render options / trace pad / microphone from `expects`, then auto-advance
once the narration has actually been heard. ExampleStrip.tsx draws the author's
own picture tokens under it.
/adventure · /rewards · /parent
Adventure is a progress board: finished, today's, sleeping until its
turn, still locked. Nothing on it starts a lesson - a second entrance
could open a level the plan has not reached. Rewards, the certificate
and the parent's progress view are read-only.
Mobile · Expo (mobile/)
useConductorClass + ClassScreen read five fields - speech,
next_input.expects, listen, auto_advance_in_ms, close - and nothing
else, which is what stops a second copy of the teaching loop growing
here. It drives the conductor, not the AI Teacher.
frontend/services/*.ts — the only place the web app talks to a server

api.ts attaches the bearer to every call · aiTeacher.ts opens the sitting and posts answers · speech.ts narrates and listens · plan.ts reads today · session.ts / auth.ts hold the parent · micStream.ts is the level meter that hears a quiet child. lib/visualIcon.ts turns an asset token into a picture, and a Hindi picture word
into the Devanagari word rather than a near-miss emoji.
2 · THE EDGE
FastAPI · backend/app/main.py
lifespan — fail loudly at boot, not in front of a child
load_curriculum() and load_skill_graph() refuse to start on malformed
authored content, naming the file. ensure_schema() creates SQLite locally;
PostgreSQL is Alembic's alone. pending_migrations() is logged and served on
/health, because a database that is merely behind breaks the schedule
silently.
app/api/deps.py — who is asking
AUTH
Authorization: Bearer, or X-Demo-Session - the same string, the
second kept so shipped clients are not signed out by a rename.
jwt_service verifies HS256 with a pinned algorithm, issuer, audience
and expiry, so a forged or expired token is refused before any query
is made.
… and the row behind it still rules
The jti claim names an auth_sessions row and that row is checked on
every request: a stateless token cannot be signed out, and sign-out
and password reset both have to actually end the session. JWT_SECRET
has no default - outside development an unset key closes sign-in
rather than signing with something guessable.
the routers — app/api/
auth · children · curriculum · plans · progress · history · speech · guide · companion ·
dev, plus the three that teach: playground (the AI Teacher: /{child_id}/open,
/sessions/{id}/answer, /ask), conductor (the mobile class), and learning / practice,
kept for older clients and marked deprecated. policy carries the kill switch: POST
/policy/disable wants POLICY_ADMIN_TOKEN in an X-Policy-Token header outside
development, because a switch that needs no deploy is also a switch anybody can reach.
3 · LOOP A — THE DAY IS PLANNED
overnight, on a timer, and no model touches any part of it
planner_runner.sweep()
BACKGROUND
Runs itself every PLANNER_INTERVAL_SECONDS (900) and
freezes a plan for every child who has none for today, so
the agent's latency is never in front of a waiting
three-year-old. Idempotent: the freeze is a unique
constraint, not this code.
plan_service._candidates()
Exactly one level per subject - the first weak one, else
the first unfinished unlocked one - and never two from the
same subject. Every subject is in every day: three stages
for Play Group, six for Nursery and UKG. No rotation, no
sample.
app/ai/planner/graph.py — LangGraph, all pure Python
NO MODEL
gather → order → freeze. There was a model here once, asked for an
ordering and fenced by a validator that dropped anything off-menu;
the fence held and the model went anyway, because ordering a handful
of known topics is a small decision with a rule that can be read.
The order is three rules: open on a level the child will get right,
meet the shaky ones early but never first, finish on a win.
daily_plans + daily_plan_items
One frozen plan per child per day, and `source` is
always 'deterministic'. The cursor is
daily_plan_items.completed_at, written by the award -
never inferred from the child's lifetime list, because
a revisit item is already in that list and such a day
arrived ticked.
plan_service.may_open()
THE GATE
A topic opens if today's frozen plan holds it, or the
child has already finished it. Everything else is
tomorrow's - including the level this very lesson has
just unlocked. With no plan at all the gate opens, so
infrastructure can never lock a child out. Refusals
read NOT_TODAYS_PLAN, worded for a child.
4 · LOOP B — THE CLASS, AND ONE TEACHING TURN
app/playground/ — the web app's teaching loop, and the only place in the product a language model runs
service.open_session()
Snapshots today's plan into playground_sessions.plan_topics and teaches them
in order, resuming at the plan cursor so a child who did two stages and
stopped picks the rest up later the same day. _class_intro says hello once a
sitting - a reload teaches the step again without re-introducing the class.
A sitting whose plan_date is not today is yesterday's and is closed, not
resumed.
lesson.py — the shape of a stage
5 QUESTIONS · NO SCORE
explain → say_it → draw → match → quiz. A stage is one item of today's plan
- one subject - and five settled questions. Every question gets three turns:
it is asked; a wrong answer brings the hint, the thing explained more deeply
ending in a clue and two or three choices; a second wrong answer brings the
answer, told and explained. That third turn expects “ready”, is never
marked, and writes no attempt.
service._recent_turns()
playground_turns is read back into the model's context, so a hint cannot
repeat its own explanation word for word. It is a reminder and nothing else:
the step, the strategy and the authored question still decide what a turn
is, and nothing downstream of a star may read it.
status = “day_complete”
THE LOCK
The last stage through ends the day. That row plus
plan_service.is_day_complete is the lock: the class will not reopen until
tomorrow's plan exists, and a reload cannot get past it because the refusal
is the server's. There is no score anywhere on the child's screen - five
dots for five questions, and which level of the day.
A · WHICH WAY TO TEACH IT — teaching_policy_service.decide()
candidates → eligibility filter → epsilon-greedy → strategy, and that order is the fence
candidates — app/policy/actions.py
The nine strategies: TELL · SHOW · EXAMPLE · STORY · CONTRAST ·
DO_TOGETHER · SENSE_SWITCH · PREREQUISITE · PARK. Early mode keeps the
five that assume no verbal reasoning.
eligibility.decide() — a separate step, before exploration
THE FENCE
Removes what the app's own rules forbid: parking a child early, an explanation
already spent on this question, a strategy the age band excludes, a prerequisite
that does not exist, a story for a child near tears. The selector only ever sees
the survivors, so exploration cannot reach a filtered action. It never returns
nothing - a repeat beats a blank turn.
selector.choose() — epsilon-greedy, 0.08, over the survivors only
A Q-table keyed on mode|mastery|rung|spent - the child's identity is deliberately
not in it. The hand-written ladder is the prior and decays as visits arrive, so
day one reproduces today's behaviour exactly. A question gets three repairs and
each is a different turn; the last one simplifies instead of re-explaining.
rollout.arm_for() + health.breaker
KILL SWITCH
POLICY_MODE is shadow in production: the ladder teaches, the table's
pick is written beside it, and nothing a child hears changes. `on`
plus POLICY_ROLLOUT_FRACTION walks 0.05 → 1.0 by a stable hash of the
child id, so nobody swaps arms mid-sitting. `off`, POST
/policy/disable, and five consecutive failures each send every child
back to the ladder without a deploy.
B · WHAT TO SAY — retrieval, the authored syllabus, and the agent
the only outbound model call in the product — and every caller already holds an answer without it
rag.search() — teacher_notes.md + the syllabus
Free HuggingFace MiniLM embeddings and cosine similarity,
with a keyword fallback that is not an afterthought. Fenced
on class_id, or the nearest passage to “letters” in the whole
index is a UKG one - and that fence holds on the keyword path
too. The answer keys - correct_answer, accept, options - are
never indexed: a model holding the key is one that can give
it away.
questions.pick() — written for this child's class
On the steps where the child chooses (match, quiz) the
question, its answer and its choices come from the authored
syllabus for the child's own class, and the model writes only
the explanation that leads into it. A topic's title is not a
question: “can you show me pre-writing strokes?” is a
heading, and a two-year-old cannot show anybody one.
app/playground/agent.py — a LangGraph graph
MODEL
START → retrieve → choose → teach → END. Only `teach` calls
out, and it asks for two things at once: the explanation in
the chosen strategy, and one question on it. The explaining
turn is three or four sentences with an everyday example in
it - what the thing is, said again in other words, something
the child has seen for themselves - because a label is not a
lesson. The same nodes run the hint and the reveal, and
neither invents a question.
app/ai/llm/client.py
BREAKER
One provider-agnostic call with a circuit breaker in
front of it. Groq · openai/gpt-oss-120b, a 6s timeout,
no retries, over one pooled connection - the TLS
handshake per call was most of what “the AI is slow”
meant. Three failures in a row and it fails fast for a
minute.
… or the deterministic teacher
ALWAYS READY
No key, a timeout, an HTTP error or a malformed body
raises LLMUnavailable, and the child still gets several
sentences out of the author's own passages, one
hand-written everyday example, a question and its
options. Failure here is normal and quiet.
on failure
HuggingFace · all-MiniLM-L6-v2
Groq · openai/gpt-oss-120b
C · COMPOSE THE DIRECTIVE — everything below this line is pure Python again
safety_service.safe_text() · leak.classify()
VETO
safe_text filters the words, so an off-topic “ask me anything” comes back as a kind
redirection. leak.classify tells scaffolding and a partial clue apart from handing
the answer over, and only an outright leak sets answer_leak_vetoed, which costs
more reward than a passed probe pays. A teaching turn is judged on its directive
frames alone (“the answer is X”, “tap X”), because naming the thing you are
teaching is the lesson - without that distinction one turn in eight was vetoed for
saying “This is a square”, and the table would have learned to stop explaining.
ensure_options() · hint_options()
A question that wants a tap always has something to tap: `expects: “tap”`
with an empty options list is a typing box in front of a child who cannot
type. ensure_options repairs it from what was already there, then the
author's own choices, then the concept's family, and invents nothing when
none of those exist. hint_options is built here in plain Python rather than
asked for, so a hint can never arrive without the answer among its choices.
examples.for_turn() · visuals.from_concept()
The example strip is two or three of the author's own visual_items for that
very level. Three rules hold it: an example is never a letter, number,
shape, colour or writing stroke - those are the lesson's own furniture, not
something a child has seen for themselves; it is never the answer to the
question beside it, checked with the same contains_answer the marker uses;
and a level whose author named nothing shows nothing rather than an
invented example.
commit() → policy_episodes
NO REWARD YET
One row per teaching turn, and no reward in it. The question, the rung,
how many strategies were spent, mastery either side, which arm chose
and what the other arm would have chosen, the eligible set, and the
leak verdict - that is what makes a moved table explicable afterwards.
It runs on the turn's own session (db.session.session_or): a second
session opened inside a request that already holds one waits out
SQLite's whole five-second busy timeout, on every turn.
5 · THE CHILD'S SURFACE
spoken out, tapped, traced and said back — and the class listens twice, because a recogniser gives up on a quiet child
the explanation is said, not printed
Three or four sentences for the ear, kept on screen only as
sr-only text for a reader. What the child looks at is the
picture, the question drawn large - the only words on the card -
and the example strip under it. A paragraph of English above a
two-year-old's question is not something they can read, and it
was sitting in the one piece of screen they could have used.
POST /speech/synthesize
NO MODEL
Microsoft Edge's free hi-IN-SwaraNeural, through the app's
own backend, so every install sounds the same and none
falls back to the browser's robot. One voice reads both
scripts, which is what this narration needs: English with
Devanagari quoted inside it. Text in, audio out - what is
said was decided upstream.
the child answers
tap · trace · voice, whichever the step's `expects` asked
for. There is exactly one microphone on the screen. The
auto-advance timer stays - the child is too small to press
a button - but it may only start once the narration has
actually been heard. Language tags are BCP-47 or nothing,
and the tag follows the content, not the profile.
listening twice — micStream + /transcribe
The browser's Web Speech API listens first: instant, free,
already on the machine. Its one bad failure is the one
that matters - it decides for itself when speech has
started, and a three-year-old saying “अ” under their
breath never clears that bar, so what comes back is
`no-speech` rather than “I heard something I could not
read”. Our own level meter is far more sensitive; when it
heard a voice and the browser did not, the clip is posted
to Groq's whisper-large-v3-turbo.
child_speech_service — stage one
“tree” for three, “wed” for red, “do nahi teen” - cleaned
by lookup in data/speech/kid_phonetics.json, which is why
it costs nothing and gives the same answer twice. It is
handed the options visible on screen and never the correct
answer, so a poor transcript can never be nudged towards
being right. It reports what was said; whether that is
right stays with the evaluator.
Microsoft edge-tts
Groq · whisper-large-v3-turbo
6 · MARKING AND PROGRESS
pure Python from the authored key, and the only path in the system that pays a star
stage.judge() — the answer-key boundary
NO MODEL, EVER
Marks in plain Python from the authored key and from nothing else. One rule decides
which options may be shown and which tap is right: stage.contains_answer both puts
an option on the screen and marks it, so the two cannot disagree and a child cannot
tap the server's own answer and be told they were wrong. Speech and typing keep the
generous word matching; normalise reads `standing_line` as “standing line”, because
that is what a child says. This rule matters more here than it ever did in a
sandbox, because the verdict now pays stars: a model that both sets and marks
learns to give the answer away.
history_service.record_attempt() → attempts
The one log everything downstream reads: mastery, the weak-skill list
the planner reorders on, and the conductor's own view of the child. A
teaching loop that graded an answer and kept the verdict to itself would
leave both reading a partial history. is_scored and is_marked are
different questions: a reveal is not scored and still counts against the
level; the echo is scored and never counts - speech-to-text mishears a
three-year-old constantly, and a level that failed because a microphone
did not catch a small voice is the app marking its own hardware.
award_topic_completion() — the end of a stage
THE ONLY WAY A STAR MOVES
The same deterministic scorer the conductor ends a lesson with, run on a score
computed out of that stage's own topic_correct / topic_answered, where a question
the teacher had to answer for the child counts as one that did not land. It marks
the level done, pays the manifest's stars, unlocks the next level, re-checks the
certificate and moves the plan cursor by writing daily_plan_items.completed_at.
…and Adventure catches up
Finishing a stage is the only thing that moves the Adventure
map. The newly unlocked level is not playable today: unlocking
is what a lesson earns, and when it is played is the plan's to
decide. Adventure redraws, the schedule strip redraws, and
neither of them can start anything.
7 · THE REWARD, PAID DAYS LATER
the reason this is not RLHF — nothing here can be earned inside the turn that spent the strategy
retention_service.on_attempt()
Every marked answer passes through here. It settles
whatever probe this attempt answers and schedules what
the answer earns. It runs on its own session,
deliberately: settling the fifth question of a stage
calls the award, which needs the write lock the probe
would otherwise be holding.
schedule the day-2 and day-7 probes
A correct answer schedules a probe two days out and
another at seven, and attaches every unpaid episode
that taught this skill. Nothing is paid now. The whole
point of the delay is that a child who was handed the
answer passes the turn and fails the probe.
settle_probe() — once, and inside the window
ATTRIBUTION
Refuses a probe that already has a resolved_at, so a reward
is the probe's and nobody else's and is paid exactly once. It
reaches back only ATTRIBUTION_WINDOW (7 days) for the
episodes it pays, so June's retention result cannot be
credited to April's teaching.
the reward, and the Q update → policy_q_values
+1.0 for a passed retention probe, +0.35 for transfer, −0.5 for
a failed one, and −1.5 for an answer leak - which is why a
vetoed turn costs more than a passed probe pays. Q ← Q + 0.15 ·
(r + 0.85 · maxQ′ − Q). Deliberately conservative: this policy
teaches real children while it learns, so it moves slowly and
explores rarely.
policy/evaluate.py — the claim nobody makes yet
OFF-POLICY
Replays the recorded episodes to compare the hand-written
ladder, random, and Q-learning, and reports “no difference
demonstrated” until the evidence clears two standard errors.
Do not claim the learned policy is better until it does.
/policy/metrics and /policy/health serve the same numbers
live.
the moved table is read by selector.choose() on the next teaching turn — this is the only feedback edge in the whole system
8 · LOOP C — THE CONDUCTOR
app/conductor/ — the mobile app's class. Same rules, different client; nothing in frontend/ mounts it any more
POST /conductor/{child_id}/open · …/input
One row in lesson_states is the live lesson, and those two
endpoints drive the whole sitting. conductor_service holds
the state, writes the truth and asks the guide for the
words. The client renders a ConductorDirective and reports
what the child did - it decides nothing, including what
silence means.
branch.py — a pure function
IMPORT-FENCED
Advance, re-explain, simplify, drop to a prerequisite,
switch modality, stop kindly. MAX_ATTEMPTS_ON_ONE_QUESTION
is 3 and each is a different turn, the last simplifying
rather than re-explaining. Running out is ADVANCE with
reason attempts_exhausted: nothing is celebrated, the skill
is marked weak, and the lesson carries on. Only a
frustrated child or an overrunning sitting ends it.
echo.py — the class stops and listens
After a thing is explained the child says it back. Three
boundaries hold it: only in subjects that teach an alphabet
or numbers, and only for a letter or a number in either
script - never a colour, a shape or a whole word; teaching
cards only, so a microphone is never open beside an answer
key; and an echo is never scored - no attempt, no star.
Asked once a sitting. Judged by string work over a cleaned
transcript, never a model.
unexpected.py — not every utterance is an answer
“Pata nahi”, the question read back, a story about a dog,
“I want mumma” - each is named and each says what the class
should do, and none of the answers is “wrong”. An utterance
that does not resolve to an answer is never recorded as a
failed attempt. Anything visible on screen is always an
answer and goes straight to the evaluator; the classifier
never sees the answer key.
signals · scaffold · skill_graph · explain
Frustration and idle watchers, the scaffolding ladder, the
authored prerequisite graph loaded at boot, and
explain.spoken_form(), which reads the Devanagari back out
of the author's prompt so the guide says “अनार” and never
the asset token “anar”.
9 · THE DURABLE TRUTH
PostgreSQL · schema in app/db/models.py, access in app/db/repositories/, migrations in backend/alembic — `alembic upgrade head`
who is here
parents · auth_sessions · auth_throttle · password_resets ·
children · child_progress. A parent's email and a child's
first name and birth month is the whole of the personal
data; consent_granted_at is written by the parent surface
only, because DPDP and COPPA both require an explicit act
by a person.
what happened
attempts · skill_mastery · topic_memories · certificates.
attempts is the single log: mastery is computed from it,
the weak-skill list the planner reorders on is read off it,
and both teaching loops write to it through
history_service.
what today is
daily_plans · daily_plan_items. One frozen plan per child
per day, source always 'deterministic'. A change to how the
day is built is invisible until tomorrow unless today's
rows are deleted and allowed to re-freeze.
what was taught
lesson_states (the conductor's live lesson) ·
playground_sessions · playground_turns (the AI Teacher's
sitting, and the only memory a turn has of the one before
it) · teaching_events, which is what was spent so it is not
spent twice.
what was learned
policy_episodes · retention_probes · policy_q_values. The
episode is written at the turn with no reward in it, the
probe is settled days later, and the Q-value is the only
row of the three that a future turn reads back.

Tests run on in-memory SQLite; the models use portable SQLAlchemy types, so one migration describes both backends. The only module-level dicts left anywhere are the in-flight lesson and practice cursors, which are rebuilt by starting again.
THE ONE RULE THAT NEVER MOVES — and the four consequences that fall out of it
▸ No language model decides correctness, scoring, stars, unlocking or certificate eligibility.

Not the branch decision either: app/conductor/branch.py is a pure function and may not import app.ai or app.services. “100% AI” means zero manual decisions on the child's surface — no navigation, no menus, no “next” button — not that a model grades anything.
▸ A reward is paid by retention days later, and by nothing else.

A reward defined on “the child answered correctly” trains a teacher that hands over the answer. That is why RLHF was rejected here, and a Q-learning reward built the same way fails identically. The probe is the only thing that pays.
▸ The fence is the order of the flow, not a check at the end.

candidates → eligibility filter → epsilon-greedy → strategy. Because the filter runs first, exploration cannot reach a strategy the app's own rules forbid — there is no path by which an illegal action is chosen and then caught.
▸ Every model call already has its answer ready without the model.

No key, a timeout, an HTTP error or a malformed body is a normal, quiet outcome: the deterministic teacher explains from the author's own passages, and a database that will not answer falls back to the hand-written ladder rather than erroring onto a child's screen.
▸ There is one way into a lesson, and the day's plan is the gate.

Not from a subject card, not from a level node, not from the schedule strip. A second entrance can open a level the plan has not reached, which is the one thing the gate exists to prevent. The level a lesson unlocks is played tomorrow.
Saksham IQ · system design · generated from the modules named above · every arrow is a call in this repository, and the six colours are the only thing that had to be added.
